title: Effects of a Novel Perturbation Balance Training Program on Laboratory and Real-World Trip-Induced Losses of Balance and Falls Among Balance-Impaired Older Adults
official: Effects of a Novel Perturbation Balance Training Program on Laboratory and Real-World Trip-Induced Losses of Balance and Falls Among Balance-Impaired Older Adults
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if a novel balance training stepping exercise can reduce the risk of falling among adults over the age of 65. The main question it aims to answer is:

* Does the novel stepping exercise improve laboratory-based measurements of balance and fall rate?
* Does the novel stepping exercise improve real-world measurements of balance and fall rate?

Researchers will compare the novel stepping exercise to 1) a more established stepping exercise that requires more expensive equipment, and 2) a more established general exercise program focusing on strength and standing balance without stepping.

Participants will:

* complete their assigned exercise intervention twice a week for three weeks, then complete booster sessions of their assigned exercise intervention once a month during months 1-5 after completing the initial three weeks of intervention
* complete laboratory sessions to test their balance: a) before intervention, b) 1 week after intervention, and c) 6 months after intervention
* use a wearable sensor daily for 12 months after intervention to capture any loss of balance or fall events
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age ≥ 65 years
* Moderate balance impairment as indicated by best unipedal stance time \<10 seconds
* Able to ambulate household distances and tolerate testing and training without an assistive device
* No significant cognitive impairment (telephone Montreal Cognitive Assessment \>18)
* Functional vision and hearing (with correction if needed)
* Comprehension of written and spoken English
* Willing and able to study-required voice recorders
* Limited physical activity (\<150 min/week moderate-vigorous), not in physical therapy, not presently in balance training programs (such as Tai Chi training).
* Not having acute or chronic conditions which would significantly alter study participation and markedly bias the results: active or symptomatic cardiopulmonary conditions; active or unstable metabolic conditions such as labile glycemic control; alcohol intake \>3 oz/day; hemiplegia or lower limb amputation; acute medical conditions, such as acute flare-up of joint condition or infection; significant orthopedic or musculoskeletal condition that does not allow weight bearing.
* Osteoporosis screening (only for subjects exposed to lab-induced trip): bone mineral density t-score \> -2.5 and no history of fragility fracture of the hip, spine, or wrist.
sponsor: Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University
